title: Introduce batch-pattern compiler and compact quant telemetry
author: Alyssa Chen
description: Motivation: Tenant workloads show recurring micro-patterns that are not well captured by the existing static batch templates. This PR adds a batch-pattern compiler that consumes recent request traces and emits compact, tenant-scoped batching templates plus a paired compact quantization profile telemetry pipeline so the Optimize layer can recommend lower-cost model variants without losing quality. Scope: 1) batch-pattern compiler service (server component and CLI to compile patterns from trace snapshots); 2) compact quant telemetry exporter that aggregates per-pattern token distributions and per-model quantization sensitivity metrics; 3) lightweight simulation harness used by CI to validate unit economics vs baseline; 4) minimal Console integration: a read-only API endpoint surfaces the top-3 generated patterns for a tenant. Implementation notes: the compiler is conservative by default (max batch-size delta +/− 20%) and emits safe fallbacks. The telemetry export uses a compact protobuf envelope and ships via the existing telemetry pipeline with optional batching disabled for immediate visibility. Rollout plan: staged deploy to canary tenant group -> 48h metrics observe window -> ramp to 20% -> full. Includes feature flag redwood.features.batch_pattern_compiler and a tenant opt-in tag. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (ENG-4572) - [x] Compiler server + CLI - [x] Telemetry exporter + aggregator - [x] CI harness and smoke bench - [x] Console API + minimal UI stub - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs: runbook and operator notes What this PR is not: it does not change default batching in production (only suggests defaults via Optimize), it does not auto-apply quant profiles without a manual review. Backwards compatibility: existing batch templates remain untouched; compiler outputs are stored under tenant preference namespace v2. Related work: ENG-4572 (design), ENG-5031 (Optimize integration), SUP-1209 (customer request), RFC-2025 (telemetry envelope). Risks & mitigations: risk of overaggressive batching -> mitigated by conservative deltas and canary. Risk of telemetry volume -> mitigated by compact envelope, sampling, and off-peak upload window. QA notes: simulation harness compares cost-per-100k-tokens and p95 latency against mainline presets and fails CI if cost drops >30% with latency increase >15%. Merge: squash. Release notes included below.

review_comments: Diego Morales: Can we guarantee the compiler will not increase median latency for small payloads? Suggest a regression test in sim harness.
Alyssa Chen: Added a latency regression check to CI harness; compiler has a small-sample guard that forces fallback to tenant preset for payloads < 64 tokens.
Priya Singh: Telemetry envelope looks good but we need retention spec; please add TTL and sampling notes to runbook.
Alyssa Chen: Added TTL=30d by default and sampling config. Updated docs/oncall/batch-pattern-runbook.md.
Evan Brooks: Code looks good, minor nit on variable naming in compact_aggregator_service.go (renamed in follow-up commit). Approved.
release_notes: Introduce batch-pattern compiler: generates tenant-specific batching templates and compact quant telemetry to enable Optimize to recommend cost-saving model/quant profiles. Rollout is gated behind a feature flag and tenant opt-in. No automatic changes to production batching; operators can review recommended patterns in the Console. Includes CI simulation harness to prevent regressions.
discussion_thread: Final approval after CI was green and bench smoke passed. Diego and Priya signed off after latency & TTL mitigations were added. Plan: canary deploy 2026-03-02, observe 48h, ramp per runbook.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag: redwood.features.batch_pattern_compiler. Tenant opt-in via tag 'batch-pattern-v2'. Canary cluster and helm values updated in charts/helm/redwood-values-cost-telemetry.yml. Monitor p95 latency, token cost, and telemetry ingress volume. If regressions detected, flip feature-flag-off and rollback helm release.
approx_impact_estimate: In internal canary runs, cost per 100k tokens decreased by ~12% median with no measurable p95 latency regression; worst-case simulated tenant showed +4% p95 latency which is mitigated by conservative delta and fallback.
